title: Grass family proper rewrite — subdivided mesh with blade displacement, sloped edge curls, organic transition to floor
intent: Audit of `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/grass-variants.ts` (S176) confirms current implementation is FOUR FLAT BOXES with different vertex-colour PAINT PATTERNS — no actual mesh deformation, no blade displacement, no edge slopes, no rotation per bitmask, no transition geometry between grass and floor cells. Result is exactly what the user reported: 'тайлы не стыкуются, нет красивых краев, нет перехода от пола к траве'. This story replaces the current 4 flat-box variants with a PROPER GRASS implementation: (1) heavy mesh subdivision (10×10 grid per tile), (2) per-vertex blade-noise Y displacement so the top surface bumps like real grass, (3) sloped edges that curl DOWNWARD toward floor level on cells where grass meets non-grass, (4) edge-overhang extending 0.1 cells over the adjacent floor (the 'grass hangs over the dirt' transition), (5) bitmask-aware variant selection so edge curls happen on the RIGHT sides per neighbourhood.
rationale: Source: user feedback 2026-05-29 on shipped S176 grass — visually it reads as 'just flat green boxes coloured differently'. The S176 implementation hit the MVP gate but failed the visual-quality bar. This story is the focused rewrite — produces grass tiles that READ AS GRASS, not as 'green floor pattern'. After this lands, the same pattern propagates to other biomes (path/stone/dirt) via GDP-2026-05-29-005. Marked `should` because the current implementation IS shipped and arenas work — this is correctness-of-visual work, not new feature.
acceptanceHints: REPLACE: `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/grass-variants.ts` from S176. Current 4 builders (plain / corner-tint / centre-highlight / stripe) are deleted; new builders ship below.
DIMENSIONS — grass overlay still 1.0 × 1.0 footprint but Y goes from 0 to 0.20 cells (taller than current 0.05 to give room for blade displacement).
BASE MESH SUBDIVISION:
Each variant starts from a `BoxGeometry(1.0, 0.20, 1.0, 10, 1, 10)` — 10×10 subdivisions on the top face = 100 top-face vertices addressable individually.
Top-face vertices get Y displacement per the blade-noise function below.
Side faces (4 vertical strips) get edge-slope displacement per the bitmask.
Bottom face stays flat at Y=0.
BLADE DISPLACEMENT (all variants share):
Per top-face vertex (x, z): Y += `bladeNoise(x, z)` — a small deterministic noise function returning 0..0.06 cells.

bladeNoise implementation: simple seeded perlin / xor-shift hash → smooth small bumps. Per-vertex offset based on (x, z) — same cell at same coords = same displacement. Bombers + bombs walk on the average Y level (0.20 cells); displacement is purely visual.
Per-vertex Y noise gives 'soft grass texture' — top surface looks tufted, not flat.
Vertex colour: GRASS_PRIMARY at base, GRASS_HIGHLIGHT lerp toward higher Y (bright tips), GRASS_SHADOW lerp toward bottom (root shadow).
EDGE-SLOPE DISPLACEMENT (bitmask-dependent — this is the autotile feel):
For each of the 4 cardinal edges (N, E, S, W), check the bitmask: if THAT cardinal's bit is 0 (non-grass neighbour), the EDGE on that side gets DOWNWARD slope.
Edge-slope rule: top-face vertices within 0.15 cells of the open edge get their Y multiplied by a slope factor: Y' = Y × (distance_from_edge / 0.15). At edge: Y → 0. At 0.15 inward: Y unchanged.
This creates the GRASS-ROUNDS-DOWN-TO-THE-FLOOR-LEVEL slope on the open edge.
Combined with bitmask: variant for N-edge-only (bitmask 8 — N IS same-family, S+E+W are NOT) → S, E, W edges slope down; N edge stays full height (continues to N-neighbour grass).
OVERHANG (transition geometry):
Top-face vertices within 0.05 cells of an open edge get pulled 0.05 cells OUTWARD (X or Z direction) — grass extends slightly over the adjacent non-grass cell.
Visual: grass blades visibly DROOP over the floor on the boundary. The transition reads as organic, not as a hard line.
Combined with edge-slope: vertices both overhang OUTWARD and slope DOWNWARD — natural curl.
BITMASK-VARIANT MAPPING:
Instead of 4 collapsed variants, the new grass family ships 5 base shapes × 4 rotations = 16 visually distinct outcomes per the GDP-2026-05-29-004 rotation pattern:
Shape A (variant 0): N is closed (same-family), S+E+W open → slopes on S, E, W edges; overhang on S, E, W. Rotated 0/90/180/270 for all 4 single-edge bitmasks.
Shape B (variant 1): N+E closed (same-family), S+W open → slopes on S+W (corner). Rotated for all 4 corner bitmasks.
Shape C (variant 2): all 4 closed (surrounded) → flat top with full blade displacement, no slopes, no overhang.
Shape D (variant 3): all 4 open (isolated) → a small grass MOUND — central blade displacement, all 4 edges slope+overhang. Smaller footprint than other variants.
Shape E (variant 4): straight wall (N+S closed, E+W open OR N+S open, E+W closed) → slopes on the OPEN pair only. Rotated 0/90 for the two straight-wall bitmasks (5 + 10).
Plus the T-junction bitmasks (7, 11, 13, 14): three closed, one open → use Shape A rotated to match the open side.
TRANSITION TO ADJACENT FLOOR CELL:
The grass overlay's edge-overhang protrudes 0.05 cells OVER the adjacent floor cell. Floor cell does NOT need to change.
Where grass meets soft block / hard block: same rule — overhang extends over the block's base. Block side rendering already starts at Y=0; grass droops naturally.
Result: NO HARD SEAM between grass cell and any non-grass neighbour — vegetation visually flows over.
PROCEDURAL DETERMINISM:
bladeNoise + per-cell variant pick deterministic per (cellGx, cellGz, sceneSeed). Same arena reload = same grass.
ANIMATION (optional polish, not v1):
Vertices could pulse slightly with sin(time) — wind-like motion. Out of scope for THIS story but the displacement Y values can be wrapped in a shader uniform for future animation.
PALETTE INTERACTION:
GRASS_PRIMARY / GRASS_HIGHLIGHT / GRASS_SHADOW exposed as theme-overridable params (matching S172 theme-aware block palette pattern from GDP-2026-05-28-013).
Themes can tint grass — e.g. bunker theme might make grass yellower (dying), lab theme might make grass blue-green (lab specimen).
PROTOTYPE ARENA:

Update `grassland.scene.json` (or the closest existing grass demo): include a row of grass cells with non-grass neighbours on E and W (showing overhang on both sides) + a row of isolated grass tufts + a 3×3 grass patch demonstrating filler in the centre.
PERFORMANCE:
Each grass tile: ~100 top-face vertices + 40 side vertices + 4 bottom vertices ≈ 144 vertices vs 24 in S176. 6× the geometry per cell.
At 100 grass cells in an arena: 14400 grass-vertices vs 2400 today. Still well under per-frame budget (~50k vertices for full scene is fine).
No new draw calls — single mesh entity per cell.
TESTS:
buildGrassVariant returns BufferGeometry with 144+ vertices (not 24).
Top-face vertices have non-zero Y displacement from base 0.20 (blade noise applied).
Variant for bitmask 1 (W neighbour same-family) → S, E, W edges have sloped vertices (Y < 0.20 within 0.15 of those edges).
Edge-overhang: top vertices within 0.05 of open edge have X or Z displaced outward by 0.05.
Determinism: buildGrassVariant called twice with same args → identical vertex positions.
VISUAL QA:
Load arena with grass tiles → visible bumpy grass surface, NOT a flat green box.
Grass cell adjacent to floor cell → grass visibly droops over the floor boundary, slopes down to floor level.
Two adjacent grass cells (interior of patch) → flush at the boundary, no seam visible.
Isolated grass tuft → small mound, sloped on all sides.
Long horizontal strip of grass (variant E straight-wall) → grass blades visible on the long open faces, flush on the short ends.
Photo test: take screenshot, see if user reads it as 'grass' or 'green floor pattern'. Should now read as grass.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Wind animation (mentioned above — future polish).
Per-vertex texture sampling (still vertex-colour only).
Cliff-grass top overhang (separate GDP-2026-05-29-006 for cliff faces).
Same-family-sub-variants (cell A and cell B both surrounded by grass use the same mesh + rotation — sub-variant random pick is a separate story).
Path / stone / dirt families — these get same treatment per GDP-2026-05-29-005 but with biome-specific displacement rules.
Inter-family BLENDED transitions (grass smoothly morphs into path texture). Sharp + overhang stays the rule.
